title: Evolve CIMA Review: Can It Rival the Big Brands?

takeaways.text: A BSA threaded bottom bracket, CeramicSpeed SLT headset bearings and a SRAM UDH hanger keep home servicing standard.

The six sizes use two fork offsets and three bottom-bracket drops to keep handling similar; even with the maximum 40 mm of spacers his position felt low and stretched, better suited to flexible riders than long days.
He noticed no flex climbing a steep hill, and on a rough descent it felt more planted than he expected from such a light bike.
The Di2 battery holder slipping is a known issue: the retailer had it happen once on his own bike, so extra packing may be needed.
The build costs roughly £4,000–4,500, compared with £3,599 for a Tarmac SL8 105 Di2 on alloy wheels in October 2026.
As shown (105 Di2, carbon cranks, Lun Hyper 60 mm wheels of about 1,300 g) the demo bike weighed 6.86 kg without pedals but with bottle cage and out-front mount; frame size not stated.

disclosure: The bike is Woods Cycles' demo bike, lent for the review; the description carries general affiliate-link notices.
summary: First-ride impressions and weigh-in of a UK retailer's CIMA road demo bike with Shimano 105 Di2 and 60 mm carbon wheels.
